text:
Priya (AE): Hey team — greenline POC hit a connector issue. Their Rust adapter using the SDK over a websocket proxy sees the session drop after ~60s idle. They want recommended heartbeat/keepalive pattern and confirmation whether keepalive pings count as token usage.

Aisha (Solutions): First pass: WS ping / TCP keepalive frames do NOT consume tokens. Only model generation requests consume tokens. If the proxy can be tuned to a higher idle timeout that's ideal. :thumbsup:

Ben (Runtime Eng): Exact — if you use a low-level WS ping frame or TCP keepalive, cost = 0. Avoid sending tiny generation \"noop\" requests to keep KV cache warm unless you accept token cost.

Priya (AE): If we do client-side pings every 25s will that break batching and increase per-request cost? The customer is worried about POC pricing impact.

Ben (Runtime Eng): Batching is an ingress queueing behavior for real generations. A WS ping won't touch the batching layer. Only actual generation RPCs are enqueued and batched. So keepalive via ping is safe.

Aisha (Solutions): If you can't change proxy, do client keepalive. Example (Rust):
```rust
// set TCP keepalive to 25s
socket.set_keepalive(Some(Duration::from_secs(25))); 
// for tokio-tungstenite, enable ws pings
ws_stream.send(Message::Ping(vec![])).await?;
```

Marco (Presales): One more thing — their proxy terminates after 90s of idle despite keepalive. They asked about ephemeral credential cadence. They want 5m tokens; is that okay?

Aisha (Solutions): 5m ephemeral creds are supported. Default we recommend 15m for stability, but 5m works if they implement smooth refresh. Sample refresh exchange:
```bash
# exchange refresh token for short-lived key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/refresh
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <refresh-token>'
  -d '{"scope":"inference"}'
```

deploy-bot: Note: Dedicated clusters may tear down idle sessions at ~2m by infra policy. If this customer needs longer retention for POC, please loop in eng-runtime to request a temporary config change.

Ben (Runtime Eng): Also watch out: if they use structured output or tool-calls that reload the KV cache on reconnect, they could pay for re-warming tokens. If they must re-auth and re-warm on each reconnect, consider caching prompts locally or a lightweight state checkpoint to reduce regen.

Priya (AE): Great — I'll share this guidance with Greenline and ask for proxy logs. They also asked: any minimum POC pricing or is it PAYG? @Marco

Marco (Presales): POC is normally pay-as-you-go. For heavy sustained throughput we can proposal a short reserved trial; DM me details and I'll route pricing.

Aisha (Solutions): TL;DR: prefer WS ping/TCP keepalive; avoid noop generations; increase proxy idle timeout if possible; ephemeral creds at 5m ok but 15m preferred; engage eng-runtime for cluster idle policy changes. Happy to draft a short one-page config checklist if useful. :white_check_mark:

Priya (AE): Perfect, please do the checklist and I'll attach to the POC handoff. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
